pillar_reactions.evidence: Delivered around whole-body function and longevity, with a yoga bridge aimed at his existing practice — 'Yoga is amazing. Kettlebells can incorporate a lot of those aspects of yoga... but it adds the strength, it adds the conditioning.' The prospect's verdict was lukewarm and honest: 'Yeah, it's fine. I mean, I'm already kind of doing that. It's just, I'm not putting in the 30, 40 minutes of nonstop.' He then asked a run of mechanics questions — whether it is once a day, whether stretches come separately, how it fits around his yoga and walks, and whether he needs to buy more kettlebells. The rep gave a good answer on equipment: 'I wouldn't go out and buy anything until you have the conversation with Trevor.'

The pillar that mattered most to him and the one delivered with the least information, since his diet was never asked about. The night-eating accommodation was well aimed and is the strongest moment of the pitch: 'for some people that even means allowing night-eating. Like if we're night-eating anyways, well, how do we just incorporate that as part of our diet where we don't have to stress about it too much.' He accepted it and immediately supplied his own constraints — limited red meat and problems with dairy — rather than reacting to the pillar itself. Given that he had said 'my weakness is nutrition' and 'I don't have a format for my nutrition... I need help with that', the flatness of the reaction is notable and probably reflects that nothing in the pitch could be made specific to a diet nobody had asked about.

Generated more questions than any other pillar, and one important correction. He asked whether contact is by text or video, whether he watches videos on a website or an app, whether he can use his desktop, whether he needs a tripod, and how progress would be measured. Most significantly he caught an imprecision: the rep described 'weekly group coaching calls. You can get on where you can have one-on-one support with him', and the prospect pressed — 'So all the meetings are a group. There's a bunch of us on the group and we're like, Hey, I have a question. Then this guy's like, Hey, I have a question' — and was told yes. He accepted it but it fed directly into his closing concern: 'it's digital. It's distance. It's from a distance. It's you plug me into a system with the other people.'

anchors.raw: I live off of seven to nine grand a month. So that's my budget to live off of what you think is a good amount, but, you know, life's expensive. And so I got to then go in and say, all right, that's out of my savings.
anchors.note: The most precise financial disclosure any prospect made in this batch, volunteered without being asked, and never followed up with a single question. It is genuinely ambiguous rather than obviously limiting — seven to nine thousand a month with several paid-off California properties behind it is not constrained, but the framing that $6,000 comes out of savings rather than income is what made it feel large to him. That distinction is exactly what the financial-picture questions exist to resolve and none were asked.

anchors.raw: If it were a monthly thing, and I was seeing the progress, and you guys were like, this is how much it is a month. I'd be like, all right, well, let's rock this thing for a couple months and see how I do.
anchors.note: A prospect stating the exact commercial structure that would have converted him, unprompted. It is not a price objection — he does not say $6,000 is too much, he says paying it as one upfront lump with no ability to evaluate is what he cannot do. The $1,200 love-it-or-leave-it is the closest product answer and it arrived ten minutes later without being connected back to this sentence, which is why it produced a lean rather than a close.

anchors.raw: And it's only 200 bucks, dude. And you hold on to the thing… I just signed up for the Hume band three weeks ago. So it follows my sleep and my metabolic rate and all that.
anchors.note: He is already an active buyer of health interventions and measurement: low-dose tirzepatide from a private provider, monthly blood panels he insisted on, monthly body-composition scans at $200, a Hume band, hot yoga eight times a month, and a kettlebell rack bought a few weeks ago. This is a demonstrated willingness to spend on exactly this problem and none of it was used to support the price.

anchors.raw: they wanted to put me on the meds, I'm like, I don't want to be on statins, that's why I did the TriZep, because I go, no, I'm either going to do it on my own, or get a little help, I'm not going on the statins, because once you're on those, you're kind of like on them for life
anchors.note: An unusual anchor: the alternative he has already rejected is pharmaceutical, not commercial. He has closed off the cheap medical route on principle, which leaves lifestyle intervention as his only remaining lever and makes coaching structurally more valuable to him than to most prospects. It also carries risk — the same reasoning is why he intends to stop the tirzepatide — and the rep engaged with neither side of it.

unmet_demand.want: A month-to-month subscription rather than a six-month term commitment, so he can see progress before committing further.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The programme is structurally a six-month term product and does not offer monthly. The $1,200 love-it-or-leave-it is the nearest available answer and it is a one-month entry rather than a subscription, so it partially serves the want without meeting it. Recorded as a product gap rather than positioning because the thing he asked for genuinely does not exist.

unmet_demand.want: A plan for sustaining results after coming off tirzepatide. He raised the drug four separate times and the anxiety underneath it is explicit: 'I want to know that I can do this without the trisepatide' and 'When I go off, I'm going to need help. I'm going to need to be on the right nutritional path.'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Answered with a position rather than a plan — 'Trevor's opinion is that you don't need it. Like, you can get the success you want if you just have the right protocol.' Nothing about how the transition off a GLP-1 is managed, what happens to appetite, or how the nutrition protocol would be built around that. This was the single clearest buying trigger on the call and it was converted into a statement about the drug's necessity instead of a service the programme provides.

unmet_demand.want: Programming adapted to two hip replacements and shortened Achilles tendons. He asked a specific, answerable question: 'I don't know if I, if you recommend buying a ramp board for anything like squats or anything, but I can do all the things. It's just, my Achilles are short.'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Deflected to the coach with a general reassurance — 'Chat with Trevor about it. He's worked with, I mean, at this point, he's been thousands and thousands of people with pretty much every different health condition, injury, limitation you can buy. He'll have something for that specifically.' No mechanism, no reassurance specific to hip arthroplasty and ballistic hinging, and no suggestion that a clinician be involved. Unvalidated rather than a gap because the programme may adapt properly; it is also the subject of a critical integrity flag.

unmet_demand.want: Objective body-composition and blood-marker tracking integrated into the coaching. He has monthly scans and blood panels already and wanted them used: 'he's going to know exactly what my BMI is, what my body fat percentage is... So now I have a starting point that's going to accurately measure.'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The programme tracks by progress photos and scale weight — 'Pictures is the main, main thing. You can tell just by looking at most people, you'll send progress photos and it's like, hey, yeah, you're probably 18, 19, 20% fat.' The rep did say measurements can be incorporated if available, which is the right answer, but it came after the photos answer and was not built into the pitch. For a prospect who measures monthly and refuses statins on the basis of data, methodology was the differentiator and it was underplayed.

unmet_demand.want: Follow-along video workouts he can move with in real time. 'I would like to follow a large video... I feel like I'll do better following along. Like, all right, let's go to the next one. Boom, boom.'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Mostly does not exist — 'the majority of the workouts won't be like that' — though weekly live group classes with Trevor do allow it and the rep surfaced that, which the prospect liked. A partial answer to a stated learning preference from someone who admits he loses focus eight minutes into a self-directed session, which makes it more material here than it would be for most.
